evidence: "if p1 + p2 > T"; all four solutions use this as the Phase Violation test before checking aggregate loads
affordance_in_statement: During each second ... 1. If second k contains a Snapshot chunk for database i, Vi is increased by 1. 2. If second k contains a Delta chunk for database i, Vi is set to 0.
removal_suggestion: Define the within-second order as Delta first and Snapshot second, so a Snapshot sent in the same second as a Delta is counted after the reset. Then a database with positive p1 and p2 needs only p1 + p2 - 1 seconds, invalidating the universal p1 + p2 > T test.

common_affordance: The specified Snapshot-before-Delta ordering makes every Snapshot counted toward the final tracker need a distinct second after all Delta chunks, yielding the shortcut p1 + p2 > T.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: After changing the order to Delta-before-Snapshot, it still rejects jobs whenever p1 + p2 > T, although one Delta and one Snapshot can share the final second.
Its hard-coded phase inequality is off by one under Delta-before-Snapshot ordering.
It reports a Phase Violation for cases with p1 + p2 = T + 1 even though the final Delta and Snapshot can occur in the same second.
Its early p1 + p2 phase rejection can mask the actual aggregate certificate after the update order is reversed.

recommended_edit: Swap the two tracker-update steps so that a Delta resets Vi first and a Snapshot increment occurs second in the same second; update the accompanying explanation to state that the Snapshot on that second survives the reset.
